messages:
samantha-support: Hey all, customer acct-324 reporting intermittent 502/504s hitting hosted inference (text-generation + embeddings) during high-volume batch jobs. Started ~2026-03-10T14:02:10Z. They see ~10% of requests fail.

alex.dev: Can you paste one of the failing curl traces they provided?

samantha-support: Copied from customer (redacted):
```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****' -H 'X-Customer-ID: acct-324' -H 'X-Request-Id: cust-req-8a3f' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"..."}'
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
content-type: application/json
{
  "error": "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers"
}
```

mike-sre: That error string looks like Envoy's upstream reset message. Any x-envoy-* or trace ids in headers?

samantha-support: They included X-Trace-Id: trc-7c9e and x-req-id: cust-req-8a3f in logs.

alex.dev: Ok. I pulled the edge logs for that trace window:
```
[ingress-nginx] 2026-03-10T14:02:11Z INFO "GET /v1/generate" upstream: "http://upstream-host:8080" host: "api.redwood.example" x-envoy-upstream-service-time: "-" x-envoy-reason: "UPSTREAM_RST_STREAM" x-envoy-downstream-service-cluster: "edge-ingress"
[envoy] 2026-03-10T14:02:11Z WARN upstream reset: RST_STREAM code=2, stream_id=97
```

jordan-eng: Stream reset RST_STREAM code=2 is AN_ERROR? In HTTP/2 that often means protocol error or flow control. Could be upstream closing while sending. Any OOMs on model host?

mike-sre: Checked dedicated serving pool autoscaler metrics: no clear OOMs but CPU spiked and connection count per worker hit ~98% of h2 concurrency limit on some nodes at 14:02.

alex.dev: Important detail — customer was doing large embedding batches (batch size 256) and also using streaming for text-generation concurrently. Combined memory + connection pressure plausible.

ingress-bot: Detected surge: h2 concurrent streams near 100 on pool edge-az1 between 14:01:50Z-14:03:00Z.

samantha-support: Customer asks if this is a regression — they said this started after we rolled the new quantized model variant last week.

jordan-eng: Are those model variants using different chunked-response behavior? Some quantized runtimes flush earlier/close sessions differently.

alex.dev: I looked at the canary rollout logs — the new variant has a slight change: it returns a premature FIN on some error paths when KV cache lookup fails. We saw a handful of failed handshakes where the model server closed the connection without completing headers. Envoy treats that as RST/stream reset.

mike-sre: Repro steps I used locally:
1) spawn 200 parallel h2 streams to a single edge worker
2) send repeated large payloads (embedding aggregator)
3) occasionally get RST_STREAM + 502 from ingress

Command used:
```
python3 stress_h2.py --concurrency 200 --reqs 500 --payload-size 1MB --header 'X-Test: embed-burst'
```

alex.dev: Stack traces from the model pod around that time:
```
E 14:02:11 model_runtime.cpp:543 handle_request: exception: kv_cache lookup out_of_memory -> closing connection
```

jordan-eng: So sequence: heavy H2 concurrency -> model runtime hits memory pressure on certain code path -> it closes connection mid-stream -> Envoy emits RST_STREAM and returns 502 to client.

samantha-support: Customer wants workaround ASAP. What's safe to recommend?

mike-sre: Short-term options: reduce per-customer concurrency (throttle), limit batch sizes, disable streaming for embeddings, or steer traffic to a less-loaded AZ.

alex.dev: We can also temporary rollback the canary variant for that customer's region. I can push a rollback to the model pool for their tenant.

jordan-eng: Also add a defensive fix on model side to return an HTTP 500 with headers instead of abruptly closing connection. But that's code change. For immediate mitigation I'd do throttling + rollback.

deploy-bot: Rolling back model-quant-v2 -> model-quant-v1 for pool pool-serving-az1 (canary). Started 2026-03-10T14:07:15Z.

ingress-bot: Post-rollback metrics: h2 resets dropped from 9.8% -> 0.6% within 3 minutes on affected hosts.

samantha-support: I told the customer we rolled back the canary and to test. They replied 'initial checks look much better, failures reduced, thanks'.

alex.dev: Follow-ups: 1) add per-tenant throttles for concurrent streams to protect model pools; 2) add better model runtime signal handling (don't close mid-header); 3) add Envoy config to treat upstream connection close as retryable for idempotent calls; 4) add observability: instrumentation to tag RST_STREAMs with model-variant ID.

mike-sre: I'll open infra task to adjust h2 concurrency defaults and add a mitigation playbook for embedding bursts.

jordan-eng: I'll file a bug for the runtime fix and mark P1 for model-variant releases.

samantha-support: Filing with customer: incident summary, actions taken (rolled back canary, throttles recommended), next steps.

alex.dev: Thanks team. Closing thread after we confirm the long-term fixes scheduled.

samantha-support: Closing notes: affected account acct-324, root cause: model runtime prematurely closing connections under memory pressure causing Envoy upstream resets -> 502/504 to clients. Mitigation: rollback canary, throttle concurrency, runtime fix planned.
